title: Destructive capabilities, conditional modes and selected preview risk
summary: Safety annotations are generated and checked against the real CLI, including nested leaves. Distinguish destructive capability, risky optional flags and action-scoped preview results; destructive:true plus agentNotice requires explicit approval, never automatic execution.
contract: destructive:true identifies a destructive capability and requires mutates:true. It includes definition replacement, deletion and running-work cancellation, not only delete-prefixed commands.

destructive_flags lists risky optional modes such as overwrite, purge, drop and cancellation on timeout. A mode-off preview need not be destructive; selecting the risky mode carries destructive:true plus an agent confirmation notice.

destructive_scope:actions is reserved for reviewed workflows whose custom preview computes the selected actions' risk. Deployment apply create-only/no-op previews remain false; definition updates, rename/republication, deletion and force-all overwrites are true. Do not treat arbitrary missing/false metadata as proof of safety.

Native nested subcommands contain leaf-level metadata. A nested Git relation deletion is destructive without making its list command destructive. Runtime recognition uses canonical full paths. MCP destructiveHint conservatively reports potential capability, not approval; nested tool invocation interfaces are not all redesigned by this change.
safety: Always preview irreversible work, inspect exact selected scope/actions, and obtain explicit approval before removing --dry-run. Neither a metadata flag nor a preview is approval or proof of readiness. A detected AI agent receives agentNotice on destructive previews.

Git checkout preview is offline, scoped and readiness-not-checked; actual readonly checkout fails. SQL import/table-drop and statistics writes reject readonly before connecting. --drop-if-exists is dangerous and incompatible with --no-create-table. Local overwrite export is likewise blocked under readonly unless previewing.

Inputs remain validated before replacement previews. Ontology update-definition validates scope and local input requirements, then previews part paths/counts before POST. This is not a service-side schema/readiness check. No live upgrade, grant, cancellation or tenant mutation is needed to validate discovery.

Policy and tests cover explicit vocabulary, real risky flags and reviewed workflow judgment. They cannot infer every arbitrary future destructive action; new custom behavior needs a policy row and runtime tests.
